To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
glutamate/glucose cycling is a major flux (∼0 µmol min−1 g−1) in the cerebral cortical tissue of anesthetised rats and the predominant route for neurotransmitter glutamate replenishment.

glutamate/glucose cycling is a major astrocyte/neuronal metabolic flux in the brain and that anaplerosis is a significant source of glutamine synthesis in normoammonemia but becomes a more important source in hyperammonemia.

in vivo and in situ13C Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) spectroscopy, with a [5‐13 C] glucose infusion, was used to determine the rates and contributions of anapleroic flux and glutamate‐glutamine cycling to glutamine synthesis, and the rates of the neuronal and astroglial tricarboxylate cycles in the cerebral cortex.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the metabolic pathways involved in neurotransmitter metabolism, particularly glutamate/glutamate cycling, and their regulation by hyperammonemia.
elucidating the role of glutamine as a neurotransmitter precursor and the contribution of glutamine cycling in this process.
understanding the metabolic interactions of the neuronal and astroglial cell populations of the brain and how these interactions are affected by changes in the metabolic milieu.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the rate of glutamate cycling in vivo is ∼0.20–0.25 µmol/min per gram of cerebral cortex.
the glutamate/glutaminate cycle is a major metabolic pathway in cerebral cortex and that anaplerosis is a major source of nitrogen for glutamine synthesis in the cerebral cortex.
anaplerosis is the predominant pathway of glutamine synthesis during normoammonemia and hyperammonemia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

glutamate/glumate cycling is the predominant astrocyte/neuroon trafficking pathway for neurotransmitter glutamate and that under normoammonemia anaplerotic synthesis of glutamine is the major pathway of nitrogen removal from the rat cerebral cortex.

the glutamate/glutamate cycling pathway is the major metabolic flux for neurotransmitter glutamate replenishment in the brain and that anaplerosis is a major source of glutamine under normoammonemia and is increased during hyperammonemic states.

glutamate/glutarate cycling is the predominant metabolic pathway for neurotransmitter glutamate trafficking between neurons and astrocytes and anaplerosis is a major pathway of glutamine synthesis under physiological and hyperammonemic states.
The main takeaway from our work is that

glutamate cycling is the major pathway of astrocytic/neuronal trafficking of glutamate and glutamine precursors, and is a major metabolic pathway in brain, and that glutamate cycling can be measured in vivo with13C Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) Spectroscopy.
anaplerosis is a major contributor to glutamine synthesis in the rat brain, and that this flux is increased under conditions of elevated brain ammonia levels.
the glutamate/glutamate cycle, which is the main route for replenishing neurotransmitter glutamate, accounts for a significant proportion of the total brain metabolism.
